audit.whatIsWrong: Yone's Q was called 'Steel Tempest' in five places, including the nonsense phrase 'Steel Tempest-Mortal Steel chains'. His R was described twice as a knock-up. Spirit Cleave (W) was never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Steel Tempest is Yasuo's Q. Yone's Q is Mortal Steel (450 range, 4s, knocks up on the SECOND stack). Fate Sealed (R) blinks behind the last champion in a line and PULLS enemies toward him — the knock-up in his kit belongs to Q. Spirit Cleave shields him on a flat 14s cooldown, scaled by champions hit, which is exactly the burst-absorber that decides whether your cascade kills him.
audit.corrected: Mortal Steel used throughout, the knock-up moved to its second stack, Fate Sealed described as a pull, and Spirit Cleave's shield written into the level-3 phase and the Don'ts.

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Unbound was the page's stated clock but never carried a number.
audit.why: 22/19/16/13/10s. At rank 1 that is a 22-second window in which he cannot bail out of a root — the concrete version of every 'wait for its cooldown' line already on the page.
audit.corrected: 22 seconds at rank 1 written into the level-2 phase and both Do's entries.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Ryze Level 1 while its why says 'Level 1 is his'; gave Yone Level 3 while its why says it is the first trade you can win cleanly; and gave Yone First item while its why calls it the moment you can genuinely threaten him.
audit.why: Three rows rendered the opposite of the text under them. The packet chart resolves all three, and 46.52% fits a lane you lose early and claw back on mana items.
audit.corrected: Yone, Yone, Skill, Yone, Ryze, Ryze, Yone — paired full/content rows with ratings.

edits.before: Level 1 is his — Yone's Steel Tempest poke forces you to respect his range and you have only Q with no setup. Farm under the threat and stack Manaflow Band; do not walk up to E range without the wave between you. At Level 2 your W root enters the equation but Yone's Soul Unbound dash can bait it: he dives in, you burn W, and he rewinds to his body safely while your root window is gone. Save W for when Soul Unbound is visibly fading, not when he engages. Level 3 is the first real window — E onto a minion to spread Flux, then W-root when the mark bounces to him, into empowered Q; the wave itself amplifies your burst and he cannot rewind out of a root that lands mid-cascade.
edits.after: Level 1 is his — Mortal Steel pokes from 450 and you have only Q with no setup. Farm under the threat and stack Manaflow Band; do not walk into E range without the wave between you. At Level 2 your W root enters the equation but Soul Unbound baits it: he dives in, you burn W, and his spirit rewinds to the body while your root window is gone. Save W for when Soul Unbound is fading, not when he engages — it is up every 22 seconds at rank 1. Level 3 is the first real window — E onto a minion to spread Flux, then W-root when the mark bounces to him, into empowered Q. Bait Spirit Cleave's shield first, or your cascade lands on 14 seconds of absorption.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a grind you accept, not a fight you pick. Yone's Q3 knock-up into Steel Tempest-Mortal Steel chains deal more damage than your pre-item patterns, and you cannot sustain a second dive the way he can reset with Soul Unbound. Farm Phase Rush procs and play the wave: crash it under his tower, back, and deny him free pressure. Level 6 does not flip the 1v1 — Realm Warp has no combat damage — but it gives you something Yone cannot match: leave him. Warp to mid or bot when your team groups and let him either split uselessly or follow and leave top open.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a grind you accept, not a fight you pick. Two Mortal Steel stacks knock you up and the dash that follows chains straight into Spirit Cleave, which shields whatever you answer with, and you cannot reset a second dive the way Soul Unbound lets him. Farm Phase Rush procs and play the wave: crash it under his tower, back, and deny him free pressure. Level 6 does not flip the 1v1 — Realm Warp has no combat damage — but it gives you something Yone cannot match: leave him. Warp to mid or bot when your team groups and let him split uselessly or follow and leave top open.

notes: 'Steel Tempest' for Yone's Q is the same failure mode as the calibration examples — a real ability name from the wrong champion, which reads as authoritative and is not. It appeared five times. Kraken Slayer and Navori are named in inherited text as Yone's item path; not verifiable from the kits and left untouched. Soul Unbound's spirit duration is not in Riot's text, so only its cooldown was written; the page's 'punish the body he snaps back to' framing does not depend on the duration.
